title: Free Couples Kink Checklist
h1: The Couples Kink Discovery Checklist — Find Out What You Both Actually Want
subhead: A free, 90-activity couples checklist — done together, not separately — that turns the 'so... what are you into?' conversation into something that actually works.
tagline: 90 activities, 5 response options, 7 categories. The conversation starter that changes everything.
meta_description: Free couples kink checklist — 90 activities across 7 categories with 5 response options. Done together, not separately. Enter your email and get it instantly.
problem:
Most couples try to talk about kink by sort of gesturing in the general direction of what they want and hoping their partner fills in the blanks. Or someone admits to one thing and then nervously watches the other person's face. Or you're both interested but neither of you is brave enough to say what first, so you end up talking about nothing.

The Couples Kink Discovery Checklist is designed to have that conversation for you — or at least to give it a structure that doesn't involve anyone feeling put on the spot.
inside: ~90 activities across 7 categories — from very vanilla to genuinely advanced
5 response options per activity — not just yes/no. Options like yes, no, curious, only if you want it, and we should talk about this one
7 categories — sensory, power exchange, restraint, role play, service, psychological, and scene-setting
Designed to do together — this is a guided conversation tool, not a solo quiz
who_for: You've been circling a conversation and haven't found the words yet
You want a low-stakes way to find out what you both actually want without the pressure
You're already exploring and want to map the full picture together
who_not: If only one of you is curious — this works best when both people genuinely want to know
If you're looking for detailed how-to instructions — this is a discovery tool, not a technique guide

faq.q: Is this actually free or is there a catch?
faq.a: It's free. You get the checklist. You get a few follow-up emails from Mr. D with genuinely useful stuff. There are products you can buy if you want them. There's no pressure, no automatic charge, no 'free trial' that turns into something.

faq.q: What if my partner doesn't want to do this?
faq.a: Then don't push it — but also, the checklist is designed to be low-stakes. It's not 'let's have an intense conversation about our sexuality.' It's 'let's look at a list together.' Most partners who are curious but hesitant will go through a checklist. Start there.

faq.q: Is this safe to receive on my regular email?
faq.a: Subject lines are low-key. Nothing that would alarm anyone who glimpsed your inbox. The checklist itself is a PDF — it looks like a document.
